title: Measuring Young’s Modulus of Organoids Using Atomic Force Microscopy
author: Zhang, Ma, et al.

steps.title: Obtain patient consent
steps.instruction: Select patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer and obtain written informed consent from each participant before any tissue collection.

steps.title: Excise and preserve tumor tissue
steps.instruction: Surgically excise a 1 cm³ tumor tissue sample, immediately immerse it in a tissue preservation solution, and store the tube at 4 °C for transport to the laboratory.

substeps.instruction: Excise a 1 cm³ tumor tissue sample surgically.
Immerse the sample promptly in tissue preservation solution.
Store the sample at 4 °C for transportation.

steps.title: Generate organoids from tissue
steps.instruction: Upon arrival at the lab, process the preserved tissue according to the standardized organoid‑culture protocol supplied by the commercial organoid provider; organoid generation is completed within 1 week.

steps.title: Prepare stained OCT gel
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of trypan blue to 300 µL of OCT compound, then mix thoroughly by repeated pipetting to obtain a labeling mixture for the organoids.

steps.title: Import AFM force curve data
steps.instruction: Open Nanoscope Analysis software, load the collected force‑curve files (each containing a complete “Extend” and “Retract” cycle), noting that data were acquired from five locations on each organoid and a total of 100 curves will be analyzed using the Hertzian (spherical) model.

steps.title: Correct baseline of force curves
steps.instruction: Select the “Baseline Correction” tool and adjust the baseline of the non‑contact region to zero, either automatically or manually, to remove instrumental drift or offset.

substeps.instruction: Choose automatic or manual baseline correction.
Set the baseline of the non‑contact region to zero.

steps.title: Extract indentation segment
steps.instruction: Click the “Execute” command to isolate the indentation segment of each force curve for further analysis.

steps.title: Fit data to calculate elastic modulus
steps.instruction: Activate the “Indentation” tool and fit the compression segment of each curve with the Hertzian spherical model to obtain the effective elastic (Young’s) modulus for each measurement.

substeps.instruction: Fit the compression segment using the Hertzian (spherical) model.

steps.title: Plot Young’s modulus statistics
steps.instruction: Using GraphPad Prism, create a column chart that displays the average Young’s modulus of the colorectal‑cancer organoids (as shown in Figure 4).
